acceptance_criteria: AC-1: verify the three gating prerequisites (collection coordinator, safe diff, cross-vendor timeline) actually exist in the codebase and work -- name the real files/functions. If any is missing or only partially built, scope this movement down to what's genuinely buildable on top of what exists, and say so plainly rather than building on an assumed foundation.
AC-2: design + implement the webhook intake boundary: authentication, a strict schema allowlist, replay protection (nonce/timestamp-window or equivalent), dedup/cooldown.
AC-3: canonical identity resolution mapping an inbound signal's device reference to the registry's own identity model -- reuse existing identity/registry code, do not invent a parallel one.
AC-4: the trigger path must only enqueue a bounded, coordinator-managed read-only collection -- never write evidence directly from the webhook handler itself.
AC-5: tests with synthetic payloads proving replay rejection, malformed/out-of-allowlist schema rejection, dedup/cooldown behavior, and that the signal path cannot write evidence.
AC-7: if blocked on a genuine PO-only decision, RELAY_NOTE and stop; PO reviews in the morning.
